script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. APT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

A dimly lit room. A WOMAN, LUCY, in her mid-30s, stands over the countertop, peeling carrots with a knife, her eyes glassy and distant. Her reflection in the window shows her face worn and haggard.

LUCY
(To herself)
One, two, three...

Suddenly, the doorbell rings, snapping Lucy back to reality. She hesitates, then sets the carrots aside and goes to the door.

EXT. APARTMENT HALLWAY - NIGHT

Lucy opens the door to reveal an ELDERLY MAN, RALPH, holding a bouquet of flowers. He smiles warmly.

RALPH
Good evening, Lucy. I brought you these. Forgive me for the late hour.

LUCY
(surprised)
Ralph? What are you doing here?

RALPH
I wanted to talk to you, to apologize for something I did years ago.

INT. APARTMENT LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Ralph sits on the edge of the couch while Lucy stands, unsure of what to do.

LUCY
(angry)
Why now? Why do you think I want to hear your apology after all this time?

RALPH
(tearfully)
Because I've come to realize the harm I caused you, and I want to make things right.

INT. APARTMENT KITCHEN - MORNING

Lucy, looking more composed, serves Ralph breakfast. They sit at the table in awkward silence.

LUCY
So, why did you do it? Why did you hurt me so badly?

RALPH
(sighs)
I was jealous. I saw the potential in you, and I was threatened by it. I wanted to keep you from achieving greatness, to keep you with me. It was a selfish, cowardly act, and I'm truly sorry.

INT. APARTMENT LIVING ROOM - AFTERNOON

They discuss their past and what has transpired in their lives since their falling out. Lucy expresses her hurt and anger, but eventually, her resolve begins to weaken.

LUCY
I've carried this anger and resentment with me for so long. It's consuming me. I don't want to live like this anymore.

RALPH
(nods)
Forgiveness is a difficult thing, Lucy. But it's also the only way to move forward and heal.

INT. APARTMENT BEDROOM - EVENING

Lucy sits on the bed, her eyes filling with tears. She looks at the bouquet of flowers Ralph brought her, now wilting. She takes a deep breath and closes her eyes.

LUCY
(to herself)
I forgive you, Ralph. I forgive you for what you did to me.

INT. APARTMENT LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Lucy sits with Ralph, her face no longer hardened and bitter. They share stories and laughter, the tension between them dissipating.

LUCY
(smiling)
I'm glad we're able to be friends again.

RALPH
(gratefully)
Me too, Lucy. Me too.

FADE OUT.
